notes: Masculine singular perfective गया (gaya) of जाना agrees with the speaker; a female speaker says गई (gai).
Feminine singular habitual participle करती (karti) agrees with the speaker; a male speaker says करता (karta).
Feminine singular perfective participle थकी हुई (thaki hui) agrees with the speaker; masculine थका हुआ (thaka hua).

glossEn: I went to the market yesterday.
notes: Feminine singular perfective गई (gai) of जाना agrees with the speaker; a male speaker says गया (gaya).
Masculine करता agrees with the third-person subject वह (he), not the speaker; the speaker's gender is unknown.
Feminine थकी हुई agrees with the third-person subject वह (she); no first-person gender marking.
First-person dative-subject construction with invariable पसंद है; the sentence contains no gendered agreement with the speaker.
Dative-subject construction: feminine लगी agrees with the noun भूख ('hunger', grammatically feminine), not with the speaker; carries no speaker-gender information.

glossEn: Are you tired? (asked of a woman)
notes: Feminine थकी marks the ADDRESSEE (तुम), not the speaker; the speaker's gender is unknown.
Feminine possessive मेरी agrees with बहन ('sister', the referent), not with the speaker.
Feminine गई inside the quotation belongs to the quoted speaker, not the narrator; the matrix उसने कहा is itself gender-neutral.
